uncited: *   A uniform Cartesian grid $C$ of size $n \times n \times n$ cells per block.
*   A dense voxel grid $V$ storing material indices or binary signs at the grid nodes (corners).
*   A sparse set of points $S$ associated with inhomogeneous cells.
*   A polygonal mesh where vertices are the points in $S$ and connectivity is determined by the triangulation algorithm applied to the voxel data.
**Voxel Grid ($V$):** A dense 3D array of integers.
$v_{i,j,k}$ represents the material index or sign (inside/outside) at the node $(i,j,k)$, which corresponds to the corners of cell $c_{i,j,k}$.
**Point Cloud ($S$):** A sparse 3D array of 3D vectors.
$p_{i,j,k}$ is the position of a sharp vertex located inside cell $c_{i,j,k}$.
A cell is **inhomogeneous** if its corners do not have identical materials or signs.
*   **Ghost Cells:** To handle boundary conditions, layers of dummy cells are added.
Iterate through all cells $c_{i,j,k}$ in the grid $C$.
A cell is marked as a boundary (inhomogeneous) cell if the values $v_{i,j,k}$ at its eight corners are not all identical.
Connect the stored sharp vertices to form a polygonal mesh.
Dual triangulation methods have inter-cell dependencies.
Hermite data (intersection points and unit surface normals) is not stored explicitly.
Identify vertices in active cells affected by smoothing.
Shift the position of a vertex to the center of mass of vertices from neighboring active cells.
**Constraint:** Average only vertices from neighbors that share an **active face** with the current cell.
The dense voxel grid dominates memory, while the point cloud is sparse.
Point Implicit Contouring was proposed as a representation for voxel terrains in virtual reality systems.
